questions.enonce_markdown:
Identify a metal

(i) Which dissolves in cold water to form an alkali.

(ii) Which will form a blue hydrated compound.

(iii) Whose ions cause hardness in water.

(iv) Which is used as a catalyst. *[4 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **Sodium** (or potassium): it reacts with cold water to give an alkali, $2\mathrm{Na} + 2\mathrm{H_2O} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{NaOH} + \mathrm{H_2}$.

(ii) **Copper**: copper(II) sulphate crystallises as the blue hydrate $\mathrm{CuSO_4\cdot5H_2O}$.

(iii) **Magnesium**: $\mathrm{Mg^{2+}}$ ions (like $\mathrm{Ca^{2+}}$) make water hard because they form scum with soap.

(iv) **Iron**: it is the catalyst in the Haber process, $\mathrm{N_2} + 3\mathrm{H_2} \rightleftharpoons 2\mathrm{NH_3}$.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) State the method by which copper is extracted.

(ii) Give the main ore from which copper is extracted.

(iii) Write a balanced equation for the main process of the extraction. *[4 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) The ore is concentrated by **froth flotation**, then **roasted/smelted in air** to give copper by reduction of the copper compounds; the impure copper is finally purified by **electrolysis** (electrolytic refining).

(ii) The main ore is **copper pyrites** (chalcopyrite), $\mathrm{CuFeS_2}$.

(iii) In the furnace the copper(I) sulphide formed reacts with oxygen of the air to give copper:

$\mathrm{Cu_2S} + \mathrm{O_2} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{Cu} + \mathrm{SO_2}$

Check: 2 Cu, 1 S and 2 O on each side. (For an oxide or carbonate ore such as malachite, the equivalent reduction is $2\mathrm{CuO} + \mathrm{C} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{Cu} + \mathrm{CO_2}$.)

questions.enonce_markdown: Give two uses of copper related to its properties. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
1. **Electrical wiring and cables**: copper is an excellent conductor of electricity and is ductile (it can be drawn into wires).

2. **Cooking pots, boilers and water pipes**: copper is a good conductor of heat and does not corrode easily.
